Hi Grace / Aditya,

- Can you confirm whether control-plane outbound egress from the on-prem runtime originates from the management plane subnets or the tenant-data subnets? We need this for our firewall rules.
- We need an explicit mapping of which ports & FQDNs will require TLS inspection exceptions (if any), and whether persistent outbound connections are used (keepalives/KV cache sync).
- Are there recommended NAT/route table patterns for multi-AZ racks to ensure failover without route flapping?
- Finally, we need a short reference diagram (single page) showing the control plane -> data plane handoff and the backplane routing (label control vs data).

Could you attach the diagram and an ops runbook excerpt we can share with our infrastructure team?

Appreciate it — we are aiming to finish firewall baselining by end of week.

Hi Donna — thanks for the clear list. Putting answers inline and attaching the single-page reference diagram + ops excerpt you requested. Short summary up top: control-plane egress originates from the control-management subnets and is strictly separated from tenant data; data-plane egress stays within your tenant VLANs unless explicit egress to external services is configured.

Answers (high level):
- Control-plane origin: management control subnets (we run the control agent in the control plane instances). These originate from the management CIDR you provide and use persistent TLS connections to Redwood control endpoints (mutual TLS).
- Ports/FQDNs: primary outbound is TCP 443 to control.redwood-inference.com and a small set of telemetry endpoints. No plaintext; TLS 1.3 with mTLS is supported. See attached matrix.
- Persistence: yes — agents keep a persistent TLS session for heartbeats and KV cache invalidate events. Idle keepalive interval configurable (default 60s).
- NAT/route pattern: recommend per-rack SNAT with short route preference and BFD disabled for the redwood overlay; we include an HA IP failover example in the second page of the diagram.

Attachments: vpc-backplane-diagram-v3.pdf (single page reference), controlplane-egress-matrix.xlsx (ports and hostnames), ops-runbook-vpc.md (excerpt).

I pasted the single-page diagram summary below for quick copy into your firewall ticket. If you want, we can do a 30-minute sync with your network team to walkthrough the runbook.

---- Diagram summary (text) ----
Control plane: management-AZ subnet (mTLS outbound) -> Redwood control endpoints (regional)
Data plane: tenant-AZ subnets -> internal backplane overlay (VXLAN) -> tenant egress gateway (customer controlled)
Handoff: control -> data via gRPC over mTLS; KV cache paths are one-way from control to data nodes for cache priming
---- end summary ----

Thanks — I'll be available for a quick sync tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Grace O'Connor

Donna — quick technical addendum from the runtime team with a few operational clarifications and a recommended snippet for your ACLs. TL;DR: control-plane egress uses the management subnet IPs we provision during install; include a CIDR range for management, and allow outbound 443 to the FQDNs in the matrix.

Operational notes:
- Keepalive/RTT: agent keepalive default is 60s; we recommend firewall state timers > 120s to avoid premature state teardown under jitter.
- TCP options: we open long-lived connections; ideally avoid L7 proxying that terminates TLS. If an inspection appliance MUST terminate, please ensure we can present the original client cert to reconstruct mTLS — otherwise request an explicit exception for control plane flows.
- KV cache sizing: in the attached diagram I annotated the backplane path where KV updates flow. This is important for your egress capacity planning during large model rollouts (e.g., warm starts).

Suggested ACL snippet (example):
# Allow control outbound
permit tcp management-subnet any eq 443 dstdomain control.redwood-inference.com
# Allow agent telemetry
permit tcp management-subnet any eq 443 dstdomain telemetry.redwood-inference.com

If helpful, I can provide an iptables/nftables sample for on-prem edge boxes. Also flagging that we support a customer-managed egress gateway if Acme needs all external egress to go through a controlled appliance — we can integrate with that model.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Manager, Runtime Engineering
